findings.evidence: template/scripts/agent_doctor.py main(): `level, message = pending_rollout_report(rollout_outcome, branch, rollout_preflight.rollout_deferred(os.environ))`. There is no try/except, and the tests only cover the error through start_task.
findings.summary: agent_doctor.py calls rollout_deferred(os.environ) with no handler, so a malformed DEV_PLATFORM_DEFER_ROLLOUT value surfaces as a raw RolloutDeferralError traceback when the doctor runs standalone. start_task catches it as a RuntimeError, so the start path is unaffected.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/rollout_preflight.py apply_defer_rollout: `os.environ[DEFER_ROLLOUT_ENV] = "1"`. It is called from main() in four entrypoints. execute_requirement advance runs its child starts in-process, so they inherit the value, which is intended.
findings.summary: apply_defer_rollout writes os.environ permanently. That is correct for the CLI mains, but the helper has no scope or undo. If it is ever called from a long-lived or in-process caller, the deferral would persist and silently suppress later rollouts. The design says the deferral is per process and never persisted.
